dedupe_keys.name: zurs geo german insurers address level zoning system for river flooding backwater and heavy rain

description: ZÜRS Geo is the zoning system for flooding, backwater and heavy rain of the German insurance association GDV, developed after the 1997 Oder and Neisse flood and supported with VdS, which bundles insurance-relevant geodata so that insurers can assess the flood risk of any address without a site visit. It holds more than 22 million addresses from the official house coordinates of Germany, each assigned a flood hazard class (HGK 1 to 4); according to GDV's data service for the 2025 natural hazard report, 92.4% of 22.6 million addresses fall in HGK 1 and 0.4% in HGK 4, where flooding occurs statistically at least once in ten years. Coverage is all of Germany. The system is licensed to GDV member companies and used by almost all insurers for building and contents cover of natural hazards; the public sees only GDV's summary statistics, and no open licence applies. Caveats: access is limited to member insurers, and the public statistics give only the share of addresses in each hazard class. Simulation uses: address-level flood hazard classes for exposure analysis of buildings and infrastructure sites and for climate adaptation screening. Related records: the Polish flood hazard and risk maps (data-poland-isok-hydroportal-flood-hazard-risk-maps).
